title: Reconnect a bathroom-sink pop-up stopper to its rear-facing pivot rod under the basin and lift the stopper open
instruction: Lift and align the sink's pop-up stopper from inside the basin while sliding the pivot rod forward through the rear drain port and stopper eye under the basin until its ball seats, then press the rear rod down to hold the stopper open.
context: General maintenance and repair workers (O*NET 49-9071, about 1.5 million US workers across hotels, apartments, hospitals, and commercial buildings; BLS OES) and plumbers (O*NET 47-2152, about 480,000 US workers) routinely reconnect lavatory pop-up stoppers after clearing hair or replacing a seal. Because an installed vanity drain's pivot port points straight toward the rear cabinet wall behind the vertical tailpiece while the stopper's clevis eye sits hidden inside the opaque drain tee, neither hand can finish the job alone: one hand reaches into the basin from above to lift the closed stopper about 6 mm and turn its eye in line with the rear port, while the other enters the open front cabinet doorway under the basin, curves around the drain pipe to push the rear ball rod forward until the pivot ball snaps into its collar seat, and presses the rear rod down so the stopper stays propped open.
setup: Mount a 1-1/4 in lavatory pop-up drain body (Danco 80767 ABS pop-up assembly, or EU Cornat TEC317405 1-1/4 in brass waste set; 31.8 mm ID, 38.0 mm OD, 54.0 mm chrome top flange) vertically at (x = 0.375 m, y = +0.035 m) inside a benchtop 18 mm birch-plywood vanity cabinet (460 mm wide over y = -0.255..+0.205 m, open front doorway at x = 0.334 m, full-height side walls and full-height rear wall at x = 0.604..0.622 m rising to z = 0.204 m, sunken z = 0.172 m front stone basin surround x = 0.334..0.444 m, front right 9.0 mm stone counter x = 0.334..0.444 m over y = -0.255..-0.023 m at z = 0.204 m with an 8 mm birch step riser, full-width 9.0 mm clear cast-acrylic rear L-roof over x = 0.444..0.604 m, y = -0.237..+0.187 m at z = 0.204 m with a 23 mm front acrylic step lip down to z = 0.172 m closing top-down access while letting top_cam see the rod, solvent-welded 5.0 mm white ABS drop-in basin 110 x 190 x 42 mm outer / 100 x 180 x 38 mm inner with z = 0.130 m underside and centred 40 x 40 mm drain hole, and dark floor mat). Thread the 3D-printed PETG 4-slot snap-collar (collar_cad.py: 26.4 mm OD x 19.0 mm, 10.0 mm front skirt with 19.2 mm pilot bore tapped to the 80767 rear port boss thread — estimated 20.0 x 1.5 mm, checked with a thread gauge before tapping — in place of its captive nut, 9.0 mm 4-slot crown with 15.6 mm ID snap ridge ending at x = 0.417 m) finger-snug onto the z = 0.054 m rear +x port over the 88532 cone washer (ball seat x = 0.401 m). Tape holes #1-3, #5-6 on a Danco 11041 chrome stopper (132.1 mm tall, 35.6 mm head OD, 36 g; EU Cornat TEC317414 35 x 120 mm) leaving #4 (88.2 mm below seal) and set it closed on the z = 0.136 m flange (+/-1.0 mm) with its eye facing y (90 +/- 5 deg off +x). Fit the 22 x 14 x 16 mm brass clevis 68 mm behind the 18.3 mm ball on a Danco 88532 steel ball rod (150 x 5.5 mm shaft, 27.5 x 4.5 mm inner tip, 44 g with clevis) with red tape 16.0 mm behind the ball, resting retracted 32.0 +/- 1.5 mm along +x (ball x = 0.433 m, rear shaft in U-cradle x = 0.563..0.590 m). Fixed layout (object_jitter = 0); no consumables.
reset_notes: Pull the pivot rod 32.0 +/- 1.5 mm rearward (+x) out of the 4-slot PETG snap-collar until its 18.3 mm ball rests on the port start rails (x = 0.433 m) and its rear shaft sits level in the rear U-cradle (x = 0.563..0.590 m), then drop the stopper closed onto the z = 0.136 m drain flange with its cap index turned 90 +/- 5 deg so the clevis eye faces y (perpendicular to the +x rear port). Check with a 150 mm steel rule that the closed stopper gap is 0.0 +/- 1.0 mm and the front edge of the red collar tape sits 32.0 +/- 1.5 mm behind the rear collar face (x = 0.417 m), matching start_top.png through the clear acrylic rear panel. Reset takes about 20 seconds; all parts are dry rigid hardware and require no consumable replacement.
scoring: Checked on a real bench with a 150 mm steel rule, a 100 mm set square, a 30 mm clearance gauge block, and the full trial video (the whole-trial fall rule is verified from the trial video; the final photo confirms only the end state). 0.0 for the whole trial (latched permanently): if at any moment in the trial video the pivot rod's 18.3 mm ball drops below 25.0 mm over the bench or the unseated rod's rear end drops below 4.0 mm onto the cabinet floor. Lifting the stopper out during the trial is not latched (scored by its end state). Otherwise, read with both stopper and pivot_rod at rest (<= 25 mm/s) and every link/finger of both hands >= 30.0 mm clear of stopper, pivot_rod, and drain: 0.5 if the front edge of the rod's red collar mark sits within 3.5 mm of the rear collar face (x = 0.417 m, ball within 3.5 mm radially of the port throat) and the stopper sits upright in the bore (radial offset <= 4.0 mm, tilt <= 8.0 deg, cap gap in [-2.0, 22.0] mm) without meeting the 1.0 open hold; 1.0 if the rod collar mark is seated within 3.5 mm (throat radial <= 3.5 mm) and the stopper cap underside is held open between 8.0 mm and 22.0 mm above the closed flange seat (radial offset <= 3.5 mm, tilt <= 6.0 deg) for 1.0 s (20 steps at 20 Hz) with <= 2.0 mm stopper drift.
fidelity: 240 Hz PhysX rigid/compliant contacts, 20 Hz control; zero welds, pushes, or proximity latches. Full-depth counter and flush 9 mm clear cast-acrylic rear panel collide solidly in PhysX (panel hidden from renderer via mk.show so top_cam sees through it). Drain bore (31.8 mm), rear +x port, and stopper eye (8.5 x 10.0 mm) use Danco 11041/88532 sizes; 4 softened cone-washer + 4 snap-collar beads create an ~8-10 N click and ~0.43 N m hold. Water, P-trap, and faucet strap are not modeled.
